topic: Extra privileges, band edges and special bands

questions.question: Why is it not legal to transmit a 3 kHz bandwidth USB signal with a carrier frequency of 14.348 MHz?

choices.A: USB is not used on 20-meter phone
choices.B: The lower 1 kHz of the signal is outside the 20-meter band
choices.C: 14.348 MHz is outside the 20-meter band
choices.D: The upper 1 kHz of the signal is outside the 20-meter band

questions.answer: The upper 1 kHz of the signal is outside the 20-meter band

questions.question: When using a transceiver that displays the carrier frequency of phone signals, which of the following displayed frequencies represents the lowest frequency at which a properly adjusted LSB emission will be totally within the band?

choices.A: The exact lower band edge
choices.B: 300 Hz above the lower band edge
choices.C: 1 kHz above the lower band edge
choices.D: 3 kHz above the lower band edge

questions.answer: 3 kHz above the lower band edge

questions.question: What is the highest legal carrier frequency on the 20-meter band for transmitting a 2.8 kHz wide USB data signal?
May an Extra class operator answer the CQ of a station on 3.601 MHz LSB phone?

choices.A: Yes, the entire signal will be inside the SSB allocation for Extra class operators
choices.B: Yes, the displayed frequency is within the 75-meter phone band segment
choices.C: No, the sideband components will extend beyond the edge of the phone band segment
choices.D: No, US stations are not permitted to use phone emissions below 3.610 MHz

questions.answer: No, the sideband components will extend beyond the edge of the phone band segment

questions.question: Who must be in physical control of the station apparatus of an amateur station aboard any vessel or craft that is documented or registered in the United States?

choices.A: Only a person with an FCC Marine Radio license grant
choices.B: Only a person named in an amateur station license grant
choices.C: Any person holding an FCC issued amateur license or who is authorized for alien reciprocal operation
choices.D: Any person named in an amateur station license grant or a person holding an unrestricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit

questions.answer: Any person holding an FCC issued amateur license or who is authorized for alien reciprocal operation

questions.question: What is the required transmit frequency of a CW signal for channelized 60 meter operation?

choices.A: At the lowest frequency of the channel
choices.B: At the center frequency of the channel
choices.C: At the highest frequency of the channel
choices.D: On any frequency where the signal’s sidebands are within the channel

questions.answer: At the center frequency of the channel

questions.question: What is the maximum power permitted on the 2200-meter band?

choices.A: 50 watts PEP (peak envelope power)
choices.B: 100 watts PEP (peak envelope power)
choices.C: 1 watt EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power)
choices.D: 5 watts EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power)

questions.answer: 1 watt EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power)

questions.question: If a station in a message forwarding system inadvertently forwards a message that is in violation of FCC rules, who is primarily accountable for the rules violation?

choices.A: The control operator of the packet bulletin board station
choices.B: The control operator of the originating station
choices.C: The control operators of all the stations in the system
choices.D: The control operators of all the stations in the system not authenticating the source from which they accept communications

questions.answer: The control operator of the originating station

questions.question: Except in some parts of Alaska, what is the maximum power permitted on the 630-meter band?

choices.A: 50 watts PEP (peak envelope power)
choices.B: 100 watts PEP (peak envelope power)
choices.C: 1 watt EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power)
choices.D: 5 watts EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power)

questions.answer: 5 watts EIRP (equivalent isotropic radiated power)

questions.question: If an amateur station is installed aboard a ship or aircraft, what condition must be met before the station is operated?

choices.A: Its operation must be approved by the master of the ship or the pilot in command of the aircraft
choices.B: The amateur station operator must agree not to transmit when the main radio of the ship or aircraft is in use
choices.C: The amateur station must have a power supply that is completely independent of the main ship or aircraft power supply
choices.D: The amateur station must operate only in specific segments of the amateur service HF and VHF bands

questions.answer: Its operation must be approved by the master of the ship or the pilot in command of the aircraft

questions.question: What licensing is required when operating an amateur station aboard a US-registered vessel in international waters?

choices.A: Any amateur license with an FCC Marine or Aircraft endorsement
choices.B: Any FCC-issued amateur license
choices.C: Only General class or higher amateur licenses
choices.D: An unrestricted Radiotelephone Operator Permit

questions.answer: Any FCC-issued amateur license

questions.question: What is the maximum bandwidth for a data emission on 60 meters?

choices.A: 60 Hz
choices.B: 170 Hz
choices.C: 1.5 kHz
choices.D: 2.8 kHz

questions.answer: 2.8 kHz

questions.question: Which of the following apply to communications transmitted to amateur stations in foreign countries?

choices.A: Third party traffic must be limited to that intended for the exclusive use of government and non-Government Organization (NGOs) involved in emergency relief activities
choices.B: All transmissions must be in English
choices.C: Communications must be limited to those incidental to the purpose of the amateur service and remarks of a personal nature
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: Communications must be limited to those incidental to the purpose of the amateur service and remarks of a personal nature

questions.question: How long must an operator wait after filing a notification with the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) before operating on the 2200-meter or 630-meter band?

choices.A: Operators must not operate until approval is received
choices.B: Operators may operate after 30 days, providing they have not been told that their station is within 1 kilometer of PLC systems using those frequencies
choices.C: Operators may not operate until a test signal has been transmitted in coordination with the local power company
choices.D: Operations may commence immediately, and may continue unless interference is reported by the UTC

questions.answer: Operators may operate after 30 days, providing they have not been told that their station is within 1 kilometer of PLC systems using those frequencies

questions.question: What is an IARP?

choices.A: A permit that allows US amateurs to operate in certain countries of the Americas
choices.B: The internal amateur radio practices policy of the FCC
choices.C: An indication of increased antenna reflected power
choices.D: A forecast of intermittent aurora radio propagation

questions.answer: A permit that allows US amateurs to operate in certain countries of the Americas

questions.question: Under what situation may a station transmit third party communications while being automatically controlled?

choices.A: Never
choices.B: Only when transmitting RTTY or data emissions
choices.C: Only when transmitting SSB or CW
choices.D: On any mode approved by the National Telecommunication and Information Administration

questions.answer: Only when transmitting RTTY or data emissions

questions.question: Which of the following is required in order to operate in accordance with CEPT rules in foreign countries where permitted?

choices.A: You must identify in the official language of the country in which you are operating
choices.B: The US embassy must approve of your operation
choices.C: You must have a copy of FCC Public Notice DA 16-1048
choices.D: You must append "/CEPT" to your call sign

questions.answer: You must have a copy of FCC Public Notice DA 16-1048

questions.question: What notifications must be given before transmitting on the 630- or 2200-meter bands?

choices.A: A special endorsement must be requested from the FCC
choices.B: An environmental impact statement must be filed with the Department of the Interior
choices.C: Operators must inform the FAA of their intent to operate, giving their call sign and distance to the nearest runway
choices.D: Operators must inform the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) of their call sign and coordinates of the station

questions.answer: Operators must inform the Utilities Technology Council (UTC) of their call sign and coordinates of the station

questions.question: What is the maximum permissible duration of a remotely controlled station’s transmissions if its control link malfunctions?

choices.A: 30 seconds
choices.B: 3 minutes
choices.C: 5 minutes
choices.D: 10 minutes

questions.answer: 3 minutes

questions.question: What is the highest modulation index permitted at the highest modulation frequency for angle modulation below 29.0 MHz?
What is the maximum mean power level for a spurious emission below 30 MHz with respect to the fundamental emission?

choices.A: - 43 dB
choices.B: - 53 dB
choices.C: - 63 dB
choices.D: - 73 dB

questions.answer: - 43 dB

questions.question: Which of the following operating arrangements allows an FCC-licensed US citizen to operate in many European countries, and amateurs from many European countries to operate in the US?

choices.A: CEPT
choices.B: IARP
choices.C: ITU reciprocal license
choices.D: All these choices are correct

questions.answer: CEPT

questions.question: In what portion of the 630-meter band are phone emissions permitted?

choices.A: None
choices.B: Only the top 3 kHz
choices.C: Only the bottom 3 kHz
choices.D: The entire band

questions.answer: The entire band
